- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 77.5+ values), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after peaks, but fails to fully revert to historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–3 days after true price peaks.
- High variance in later days (days 20–30) suggests model underestimates volatility or fails to capture tail risk.
- Model exhibits “early overconfidence” — overestimates near the start of the forecast, then gradually underestimates later days.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to overreact with a sharp peak, then flattens too early.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the final 5–10 days, especially when true prices show upward momentum.
- Correction: reduce initial forecast peak by 2–5% and adjust later days to reflect mean reversion toward historical 30-day average.
